mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2.5% for three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% signals weakening demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during co-occurrence of GDPC1 < -2% YoY and HOUST < -10% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 3% over three consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and reduces output, leading to negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 3 consecutive months (cumulative < -3%)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during three-month INDPRO declines exceeding 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% combined with a concurrent decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 1.5% signals a deep easing cycle, which boosts risk appetite and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL < 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 10-year moving average while personal income (PAYEMS) grows below trend signals heightened precautionary saving, which reduces consumer spending and depresses earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 10-year moving average AND PAYEMS < 10-year moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of elevated savings and below-trend income growth.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as earnings expectations rise.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS grows above 0.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below 900K units for four consecutive months signals a housing market downturn, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of HOUST < 900K.
